correctness.rationale: The frozen equations are correct. Choosing unmatched sets and a bijection of the remainder gives n!(n+k)!/[j!(j+k)!(n−j)!], and the two unmatched sets are independently uniform conditional on j. With p the Bessel mass and b=(n)_j/n^j (0 beyond n), the Gibbs law is p b/E_p b. Rejection with probability 1−b, bounded by binom(j,2)/n for all j, gives the original TV bound. Shifting the Bessel sum gives factorial moments and domination gives convergence. Laguerre roots are positive and simple by orthogonality; reciprocal shifted roots give the independent Bernoulli probabilities. Strict Cauchy–Schwarz on the distinct probabilities (append k ones for the right shore) gives finite same-shore signs. Independent conditional selection gives C_LR=Var(J_n)/[n(n+k)]. The two same-shore limits follow from second factorial moments, with the right coefficient subtracting k. For strict limiting negativity, the Bessel ratio gives f_2−μ²=c Cov(J,1/(J+k+1))<0. The exact successive-weight ratios give concentration at zero above the window and escape of every fixed lower tail below it, at fixed k. Independent edge-subset enumeration at (n,k,λ)=(2,0,1),(2,1,2),(3,1,3/2),(4,2,3) reproduced all deficit weight ratios and the three signs; at (2,1,2) the respective covariances were −12/1369, −104/1369 and 66/1369. For the repaired claim set D(j)=binom(j,2). Then d_n=n(1−b) converges pointwise to D, is bounded by D, and converges in L1(p). Exactly n(p_n−p)=p(E_p d_n−d_n)/E_p b, hence convergence in l1 to p(E_p D−D). The half-norm gives the exact positive TV coefficient, since p has positive mass at j=0 and j=2. A supplementary numerical calculation at k=1,c=2 gives n TV≈0.186218389, 0.187258224, 0.187362184 for n=20,200,2000 against the limit 0.187373735; only the normalized-tilt proof certifies the infinite statement. The complete replacement files are under /workspace/repairs/5/; the original scripts were read as evidence, not executed.
